---
title: "What does PCA maximize?"
toc: false
page-layout: full
---

PCA searches for a direction that preserves as much variation as possible. Here,
you can rotate a one-dimensional view of a two-dimensional point cloud and see
how the projected values spread out.

::: {.callout-tip}
## What to watch

The purple dashed line marks **PC1**, the direction with the greatest projected
variance. The rotating line passes through the data mean. As it turns, each
point is projected onto it, and the histogram shows the resulting one-dimensional
values. The spread is greatest at PC1 and smallest at the perpendicular PC2.
:::

The points were digitized approximately from a static scatter plot. Their
coordinates are now a fixed dataset: every view and calculation on this page
uses the same observations. The marginal histograms show the original `x` and
`y` distributions; the large histogram updates with the current projection.

```{=html}
<div id="pca-explorer" class="pca-explorer" aria-label="Interactive PCA projection explorer">
  <div class="pca-toolbar clt-buttons" role="group" aria-label="PCA projection controls">
    <button id="pca-play" type="button" class="regression-sampling-primary">Play rotation</button>
    <button id="pca-reset" type="button">Show PC1</button>
    <label class="pca-angle-control" for="pca-angle">
      <span>Projection angle, θ</span>
      <input id="pca-angle" type="range" min="0" max="360" step="1" value="0" aria-describedby="pca-angle-value">
      <output id="pca-angle-value" for="pca-angle">0°</output>
    </label>
    <output id="pca-status" class="pca-status" aria-live="polite">Loading the point cloud…</output>
  </div>

  <div class="pca-workbench">
    <section class="pca-panel pca-scatter-panel" aria-labelledby="pca-scatter-heading">
      <div class="pca-panel-heading">
        <h2 id="pca-scatter-heading">Original points and their projections</h2>
        <p>The thin red segments connect each observation to its perpendicular projection on the rotating direction.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="pca-main-layout">
        <div class="pca-top-marginal">
          <svg id="pca-x-histogram" viewBox="0 0 520 110" role="img" aria-label="Static marginal histogram of original x values"></svg>
        </div>
        <div class="pca-scatter-wrap">
          <svg id="pca-scatter" viewBox="0 0 520 520" role="img" aria-label="Two-dimensional point cloud with a rotating PCA projection direction"></svg>
        </div>
        <div class="pca-side-marginal">
          <svg id="pca-y-histogram" viewBox="0 0 155 520" role="img" aria-label="Static marginal histogram of original y values"></svg>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="pca-legend" aria-label="Plot legend">
        <span><i class="pca-legend-dot"></i> Original observation</span>
        <span><i class="pca-legend-line pca-legend-projection"></i> Projection segment</span>
        <span><i class="pca-legend-line pca-legend-direction"></i> Current direction</span>
        <span><i class="pca-legend-line pca-legend-pc1"></i> PC1 reference</span>
      </div>
    </section>

    <section class="pca-panel pca-projection-panel" aria-labelledby="pca-projection-heading">
      <div class="pca-panel-heading">
        <h2 id="pca-projection-heading">Distribution after projection</h2>
        <p>Each point contributes one centered scalar value, <code>z</code>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="pca-metrics" aria-live="polite">
        <div class="pca-metric pca-current-metric">
          <span>Projected variance</span>
          <strong id="pca-variance">—</strong>
        </div>
        <div class="pca-metric">
          <span>Variance retained</span>
          <strong id="pca-variance-share">—</strong>
        </div>
      </div>
      <svg id="pca-projection-histogram" viewBox="0 0 430 440" role="img" aria-label="Histogram of values projected onto the current direction"></svg>
      <div class="pca-eigenvalues">
        <div><span>PC1 · maximum</span><strong id="pca-lambda-one">—</strong></div>
        <div><span>PC2 · minimum</span><strong id="pca-lambda-two">—</strong></div>
      </div>
      <p id="pca-orientation-note" class="pca-orientation-note" aria-live="polite"></p>
    </section>
  </div>

  <div class="pca-explanation">
    <p>For a unit direction <em>u</em><sub>θ</sub> = (cos θ, sin θ), each point is centered at the data mean and projected to <em>z</em><sub>i</sub> = (<em>x</em><sub>i</sub> − x̄) cos θ + (<em>y</em><sub>i</sub> − ȳ) sin θ. Its variance is <em>u</em><sub>θ</sub><sup>T</sup>Σ<em>u</em><sub>θ</sub>. PCA chooses the direction that maximizes this quantity; the maximum is the largest eigenvalue of the sample covariance matrix.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```
